/conditions/ankylosing-spondylitis/exerc.question: What are the best exercises for ankylosing spondylitis?
/conditions/ankylosing-spondylitis/exerc.answer: Daily spinal mobility plus low-impact cardio such as swimming are foundational for AS; treat movement as medicine and stop for sharp inflammatory pain.
/conditions/ankylosing-spondylitis/exerc.bodyHtml:
Best exercises for ankylosing spondylitis

Daily spinal mobility work is core treatment for ankylosing spondylitis (axial spondyloarthritis), not an optional extra. NASS and rheumatology teams encourage gentle extension, rotation and breathing drills most days, including quieter days when rest feels tempting.

Combine mobility with low-impact cardio such as swimming or walking, and stop short of sharp inflammatory pain. If eyes become red and painful, seek urgent ophthalmology advice for possible uveitis. Pair this page with the main AS condition guide and treatment subpage.

/supplements/turmeric.title: Is Turmeric Good for Arthritis? UK Curcumin Guide | Living With Arthritis
/supplements/turmeric.description: Honest UK guide to turmeric and curcumin for arthritis: the evidence, the right dose (around 1,000 mg/day), why black pepper matters for absorption, side effects and interactions.
/supplements/turmeric.question: Is turmeric good for arthritis?
/supplements/turmeric.answer: Trials of curcumin (around 1,000 mg/day for 8–12 weeks) show modest reductions in knee osteoarthritis pain for some people. Cooking with turmeric powder alone rarely matches trial doses. Check interactions with your GP or pharmacist. Educational guidance, not a prescription.

faqs.q: Is turmeric good for arthritis?
faqs.a: Yes, modestly. Trials of curcumin (the active compound in turmeric) at around 1,000 mg/day for 8â12 weeks show meaningful reductions in knee osteoarthritis pain and stiffness, sometimes comparable to ibuprofen or diclofenac but with fewer stomach side effects.

faqs.q: How much turmeric or curcumin should I take?
faqs.a: Clinical trials mostly use 500â1,000 mg of curcumin extract per day, usually split into two doses with food. Cooking with turmeric powder alone will not deliver that dose â supplements standardised to 95% curcuminoids are what the studies test.

faqs.q: Why is black pepper (piperine) added to turmeric supplements?
faqs.a: Curcumin is poorly absorbed on its own. Adding piperine from black pepper increases its bioavailability by up to 2,000%. Most reputable UK curcumin supplements include piperine or use a formulation like Meriva or BCM-95 that boosts absorption in other ways.

faqs.q: How long does turmeric take to work for arthritis?
faqs.a: Allow at least 8â12 weeks of daily use. If pain and stiffness have not improved by 3 months, stop â you are unlikely to be a responder.

faqs.q: What are the side effects of turmeric?
faqs.a: Turmeric is generally well tolerated. The most common issues are mild indigestion, nausea or diarrhoea. Rare cases of liver injury have been reported at high doses, so stick to standard trial doses and stop if you feel unwell.

faqs.q: Who should avoid turmeric supplements?
faqs.a: Talk to your GP before taking turmeric if you are pregnant, take blood thinners (warfarin, apixaban, aspirin), have gallstones or bile-duct problems, diabetes medication, or are due to have surgery within two weeks.

faqs.q: Turmeric vs ibuprofen for arthritis â which is better?
faqs.a: For knee osteoarthritis, head-to-head trials show curcumin roughly matches ibuprofen or diclofenac for pain relief over 4â12 weeks, with fewer stomach and kidney side effects. It is slower to act. For short flares, NSAIDs still work faster.

/guides/understanding-pain.title: Understanding Arthritis Pain | Talking to Your GP
/guides/understanding-pain.description: Understand arthritis pain: inflammatory and mechanical symptoms, nerve pain, fibromyalgia and practical questions to discuss with your GP or specialist.
/guides/understanding-pain.question: What are the main types of pain?
/guides/understanding-pain.answer: Pain can be inflammatory or mechanical, focal or systemic, bilateral, fibromyalgia-type, acute or chronic, or neuropathic. Matching the pattern helps your GP choose the right next steps. Describe location, timing, morning stiffness and nerve-like burning or tingling clearly.

/stories.title: Share Your Arthritis Story | Living With Arthritis
/stories.description: Share your experience of living with arthritis in the UK. How to send your story, how consent works, our editorial and safeguarding rules, and what to expect.
/stories.question: How can I share my arthritis story with Living With Arthritis?
/stories.answer: Email info@livingwitharthritis.org.uk with the subject 'Share my story', or use the contact form. We only publish an account you send us, after you have seen and approved the final version. You can stay anonymous and ask us to remove it at any time. No stories have been published yet: stories coming soon.

faqs.q: Do you publish stories from real patients?
faqs.a: Only real accounts sent to us by the person themselves, edited with them and approved by them in writing before publication. We have not published any yet. We never invent stories, names or quotes.

faqs.q: Can I share my story anonymously?
faqs.a: Yes. You can choose your full name, first name only, initials or no name at all. We will remove details that could identify you if you ask.

faqs.q: Can I change my mind after my story is published?
faqs.a: Yes. Email us and we will take it down or change it as soon as we can. We cannot control copies made by others before removal, which is one reason to think carefully about identifying details.

faqs.q: Will you pay me for my story?
faqs.a: No. We do not pay for stories and we do not accept payment to publish them.

faqs.q: Can I mention the treatment or products that helped me?
faqs.a: You can describe your treatment. We will not publish recommendations of specific products, private practitioners or unproven treatments, and we may add a note pointing to NHS or NICE information.

faqs.q: Can young people share their story?
faqs.a: Yes, with the written agreement of a parent or guardian if they are under 18. We take extra care with identifying details for under-18s.
